assessment_summary:
Step 1: Suppose X, Y, and Z are mutually independent real-valued random variables. (Justified setup)
Step 2: Suppose X beats Y, which means P(X > Y) > 1/2. (Justified assumption)
Step 3: Suppose Y beats Z, which means P(Y > Z) > 1/2. (Justified assumption)
Step 4: It follows that P(X > Z) > 1/2, meaning X beats Z, and thus the relation is transitive. (Unjustified)

The deduction in Step 4 is flawed. There is no mathematical law guaranteeing transitivity for the probabilistic inequality P(A > B) > 1/2 among independent random variables. This known paradox is often illustrated with non-transitive dice.
